candidates.title: Automated liver segmentation from CT images using modified ResUNet
candidates.abstract: The Segmentation of liver from computed tomography (CT) images is a critical task in medical research particularly when employing deep learning methods. Most doctors prefer to use Computed tomography images for liver disease identification hence automatic liver segmentation plays a decisive role. To perform automatic segmentation of liver popular architectures such as modified ResUNet are specifically designed to capture multi-resolution features. In this study we proposed an automatic system that utilizes convolutional layers to efficiently extract features while maintaining spatial information. A modified Residual UNet model was developed for liver segmentation using the 3Dircadb dataset, the model demonstrated excellent performance by achieving a Dice Score of 93.08% , accuracy of 98.57%, Jaccard Index of 87.12%, a volumetric overlap error of 12.87 % , and a relative volume difference of 14.91% on 128x128 size images. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed method. The primary goal of this research is to apply deep learning techniques for liver segmentation and assess the model’s performance using segmentation metrics.

candidates.title: Explainable and Robust Deep Learning for Liver Segmentation Through U-Net Network
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Clinical imaging techniques, such as magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography, play a vital role in supporting clinicians by aiding disease diagnosis and facilitating the planning of appropriate interventions. This is particularly important in malignant conditions like hepatocellular carcinoma, where accurate image segmentation, delineating the liver and tumor, is a critical initial step in optimizing diagnosis, staging, and treatment planning, including interventions like transplantation, surgical resection, radiotherapy, portal vein embolization, and other procedures. Therefore, effective segmentation methods can significantly influence both diagnostic accuracy and treatment outcomes. Method: In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach aimed at accurately segmenting the liver in medical images, thus addressing a critical need in hepatic disease diagnosis and treatment planning. We consider a U-Net architecture with residual connections to capture fine-grained anatomical details. We also take into account the prediction explainability, aiming to highlight, in the image under analysis, the areas that are symptomatic for a certain segmentation. In detail, by exploiting the U-Net architecture, two different models are trained with two annotated datasets of computed tomography medical images, resulting in four different experiments. Results: We consider two different datasets to improve robustness and generalization across diverse patient populations and imaging conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method obtains interesting performances, with an accuracy ranging from 0.81 to 0.93. Conclusions: We thus show that the proposed method can provide a reliable and efficient solution for automated liver segmentation, promising significant advancements in clinical workflows and precision medicine.

candidates.title: A Reverse Mamba Attention Network for Pathological Liver Segmentation
candidates.abstract: We present RMA-Mamba, a novel architecture that advances the capabilities of vision state space models through a specialized reverse mamba attention module (RMA). The key innovation lies in RMA-Mamba’s ability to capture long-range dependencies while maintaining precise local feature representation through its hierarchical processing pipeline. By integrating Vision Mamba (VMamba)’s efficient sequence modeling with RMA’s targeted feature refinement, our architecture achieves superior feature learning across multiple scales. This dualmechanism approach enables robust handling of complex morphological patterns while maintaining computational efficiency. We demonstrate RMA-Mamba’s effectiveness in the challenging domain of pathological liver segmentation (from both CT and MRI), where traditional segmentation approaches often fail due to tissue variations. When evaluated on a newly introduced cirrhotic liver dataset (CirrMRI600+) of T2-weighted MRI scans, RMA-Mamba achieves the state-of-the-art performance with a Dice coefficient of $92.08 \%$, mean IoU of $87.36 \%$, and recall of $\mathbf{9 2. 9 6 \%}$. The architecture’s generalizability is further validated on the cancerous liver segmentation from CT scans (LiTS: Liver Tumor Segmentation dataset), yielding a Dice score of 92.9% and $\mathbf{m I o U}$ of $\mathbf{8 8. 9 9 \%}$. The source code of the proposed RMA-Mamba is available after double blind review. Our code is available for public: https://github.com/JunZengz/RMAMamba.

candidates.title: Liver segmentation algorithm based on improved UNet
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes an improved UNet architecture (RR UNet) for liver segmentation in CT images. To address the problems of irregular liver shape and blurred boundary, the Recurrent Attention Block(RABlock) module is introduced into the decoder to enhance the feature expression ability and boundary recognition accuracy. At the same time, the Residual Skip Connection (RSC) module is used to promote multi-scale semantic information fusion, and the hybrid loss function of BCE and Focal Loss is combined to alleviate the class imbalance problem. The experimental results on the LiTS2017 dataset show that RR UNet significantly improves multiple performance indicators compared to the baseline model: mIoU reaches 95.8%, DSC rises to 87.7%, Precision is 98.6%, Recall reaches 97.1%, and ASSD drops to 3.48mm. This method effectively improves the accuracy and robustness of liver segmentation.

candidates.title: Cross modality medical image synthesis for improving liver segmentation
candidates.abstract: Deep learning-based computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) of medical images requires large datasets. However, the lack of large publicly available labelled datasets limits the development of deep learning-based CAD systems. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), in particular, CycleGAN, can be used to generate new cross-domain images without paired training data. However, most CycleGAN-based synthesis methods lack the potential to overcome alignment and asymmetry between the input and generated data. We propose a two-stage technique for the synthesis of abdominal MRI using cross-modality translation of abdominal CT. We show that the synthetic data can help improve the performance of the liver segmentation network. We increase the number of abdominal MRI images through cross-modality image transformation of unpaired CT images using a CycleGAN inspired deformation invariant network called EssNet. Subsequently, we combine the synthetic MRI images with the original MRI images and use them to improve the accuracy of the U-Net on a liver segmentation task. We train the U-Net on real MRI images and then on real and synthetic MRI images. Consequently, by comparing both scenarios, we achieve an improvement in the performance of U-Net. In summary, the improvement achieved in the Intersection over Union (IoU) is 1.17%. The results show the potential to address the data scarcity challenge in medical imaging.

candidates.title: Image Segmentation Methods in Mammography: a Literature Review
candidates.abstract: This article aims to present a systematic literature review on modern image segmentation methods in mammography. Since the 1980s, mammography has been a standard examination used to identify nodules and signs of breast cancer, being an accessible and low-cost examination. Currently, breast cancer is the most frequent type of cancer in women in Brazil. As a form of early disease control, imaging exams are an important medical ally, and in recent years technology has been used to identify lesions in images. This work was restricted to research articles that use image segmentation methods involving machine learning and deep learning. The selection adopted was of works published in the last five years in the journals: Elsevier, IEEE, Springer and MDPI. Initially, 550 articles were selected, and of these, only 51 passed the funneling stage. The literature review revealed a predominant use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), mainly U-Net and ResNet, and free databases, especially CBIS-DDSM and DDSM. In recent years, significant results have been observed with the U-Net architecture and with CNN+ Transformers integrative models. The accuracy of the models exceeds 98% in some studies, and recently, the FDA approved the use of deep learning technologies to support medical decision-making.

candidates.title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Chronic Hepatitis B
candidates.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) burdens the healthcare system, affecting millions of individuals worldwide with a potential progression to complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The World Health Organization launched the chronic viral hepatitis elimination plan which aimed to eliminate chronic hepatitis B virus by 2030, yet the goal has seemed to be far from reach with the remaining few years owing to different hurdles ranging from screening strategy and diagnosis to risk stratification for antiviral treatment and HCC surveillance. To refine the management of CHB, previous studies focused on identifying the at-risk populations and predictors for adverse outcomes using conventional statistical methods. With the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI), there is further room to improve different aspects of screening and management. For instance, generative AI, such as large language models (LLMs), has been proven to have the ability to answer different clinical questions, assisting patients' and physicians' decision on various clinical scenarios. Different machine learning and deep learning models have also been developed to assess for liver fibrosis, as well as to aid segmentation of liver structures and detection of focal liver lesions through various imaging modalities. While different AI models have shown superior performance compared to those developed through traditional statistical models, the lack of standardized datasets in training cohorts and the unresolved concerns of hallucination of false information in LLMs pose challenges on applying AI in the current management of CHB, in which further studies are required to adopt AI into daily clinical practice.

candidates.title: Quantized TotalSegmentator for Fast Abdominal Organ Segmentation on CPUs
candidates.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND TotalSegmentator is designed for a graphics processing unit (GPU), runs slowly on a central processing unit (CPU), and depends on Python, limiting CPU-only clinical deployment. OBJECTIVE The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether TS-Portable, a self-contained CPU executable running 8-bit integer (INT8)–quantized TotalSegmentator models, is noninferior to the reference implementation across 15 abdominal organs in an external multicenter cohort, quantify CPU-only runtime, and demonstrate spleen volumetry on a picture archiving and communication system (PACS) reading station. METHODS This retrospective study compared TS-Portable with the reference Python implementation on 100 external multicenter CT scans and 28 chronic liver disease series. Per-case mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 3-mm normalized surface distance (NSD@3 mm) across 15 organs (1.5-mm resolution) and spleen-only mode were tested against a 0.01 noninferiority margin (paired bootstrap 95% CIs). Workstation and PACS runtimes were recorded; spleen volumes were compared via Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS The external cohort included 100 patients (53 men, 47 women; mean age, 53 ± 16 [SD] years). Across 15 organs, TS-Portable was noninferior for mean DSC (difference, 0.00017; 95% CI, 0.00003–0.00031; p < .001) and NSD@3 mm (difference, 0.00015; 95% CI, −0.00002 to 0.00031; p < .001) and in spleen-only mode (both p < .001). Workstation 1.5-mm median runtime was 48.0 seconds for TS-Portable on CPU versus 342.5 seconds on CPU (ratio, 7.14) and 61.5 seconds on GPU (ratio, 1.28) for the reference. On PACS, CPU spleen volumetry took 5.8 versus 43.4 seconds, agreeing with the reference (CCC, 0.9999; bias, 0.2%; 95% limits of agreement, −7.2% to 7.6%) and manual contours (CCC, 0.989; bias, −6.8%). In 28 chronic liver disease series, TS-Portable ran from DICOM in 6.5 seconds (median), agreeing with the reference (CCC, 0.99999) and manual contours (CCC, 0.992; bias, −3.4%). CONCLUSION TS-Portable achieved noninferior abdominal organ segmentation accuracy compared with the reference implementation while running faster on a workstation CPU than the reference on a GPU. CLINICAL IMPACT Self-contained deployment enables fast multiorgan segmentation on CPU-only computers and spleen volumetry within seconds on a standard reading station, without dedicated GPUs or software installation. Highlights Key Finding Across 100 external multicenter CT examinations, a quantized, self-contained CPU executable of TotalSegmentator was noninferior to the reference implementation for 15-organ segmentation accuracy and 7.14-fold faster on a workstation CPU, and completed reading-station spleen volumetry in a median of 5.8 seconds. Importance Compiling and quantizing three-dimensional segmentation models into a standalone CPU executable removes GPU and software-installation barriers, enabling rapid quantitative CT analysis on standard clinical workstations.

candidates.title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
candidates.abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

candidates.title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
candidates.abstract: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

candidates.title: LIVER CANCER DETECTION USING RESNET, SWIN TRANSFORMER AND CONVNEXT TINY NETWORKS
candidates.abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. Another challenge is that slices from the same patient can be very similar, which may cause data leakage when splitting the data randomly. This study focuses on classifying liver CT slices into Tumor and No-Tumor classes using deep learning. The LiTS and 3Dircadb datasets are combined and used for the experiments. Three deep learning models, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50, are trained and evaluated. A patient-level data split is used to keep patients in the training, validation, and test sets separate. The three models are also combined using a soft-voting ensemble. The final evaluation is performed on an unseen test set containing 6,323 slices. The soft-voting ensemble achieved the highest accuracy of 92.74%. These results show that the models can detect tumor and no-tumor slices, while the class imbalance remains an important challenge for tumor detection.

candidates.title: Anatomy and Function
candidates.abstract: The liver is derived from a foregut endodermal bud, which develops in the third week of gestation and divides into two parts: hepatic and biliary. The lobule described by Kiernan is the most widely used unit of liver microanatomy, consisting of a hexagon-like region of liver parenchyma with a central vein as its hub and portal tracts located in the periphery of the hexagon. This chapter introduces the concept of functional anatomy. The Couinaud classification defines eight segments, while the Bismuth classification divides the liver into four sectors. The chapter discusses the anatomical abnormalities of the liver. The sinusoidal cells form a functional and histological unit together with the sinusoidal aspect of the hepatocyte. Bile duct epithelial cells line the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts and modify the bile derived from the canaliculi of the hepatocytes. Normal liver structure and function depend upon a balance between cell death and regeneration.
